page: UpCloud GPU-16xCPU-192GB-1xL40S is a GPU-accelerated virtual server running on the KVM hypervisor. It features 16 shared vCPUs mapped to 16 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 9575F processor operating at 2.0 GHz. The system includes 192.0 GB of system memory, providing 12.0 GB per core. Acceleration is driven by a single NVIDIA L40S GPU based on the Ada Lovelace architecture, equipped with 48 GB of VRAM. No local storage is bundled with this instance type, though it includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

CPU benchmarks indicate strong computational capabilities, with Geekbench single-core and multi-core scores placing in the top 10% tier. Single-core stress-ng performance also reaches the top 10% tier at 4172.89, while multi-core stress-ng performance is in the top 25% tier at 67220.77. Memory performance is characterized by a strong large-block read bandwidth of 329.44 GB/sec and write bandwidth of 143.42 GB/sec, both in the top 25% tier, though cached small-block read bandwidth remains in the middle 50% tier at 3196.51 GB/sec.

The hardware configuration is optimized for machine learning and data processing tasks. In LLM inference benchmarks using a small 135M model, the server achieves top-tier performance with 3898.64 tokens/sec for prompt processing and 386.1 tokens/sec for text generation. For a medium 7B model, text generation reaches 36.41 tokens/sec, while prompt processing operates at 124.61 tokens/sec. Large 70B model inference yields 12.03 tokens/sec for prompt processing and 3.88 tokens/sec for text generation, reflecting the resource limits of a single GPU setup for very large parameters.

The primary tradeoff of this instance is the shared CPU allocation and the complete absence of local storage, requiring external storage attachments for persistent data. However, the high memory-to-core ratio and the 48 GB GPU VRAM make it highly cost-efficient for GPU-accelerated workloads that do not require dedicated CPU pinning. This server is suited for small-to-medium LLM inference, image processing, and parallelized scientific computing.
